2608.30754.title: CLIN: an Objective Framework for Evaluating Creativity in Short Persian Literary Text
2608.30754.paper_summary: Evaluating creativity in large language model (LLM) outputs remains challenging because creativity is multidimensional and human-centered. We examine how reliably LLMs evaluate short literary text in Persian, a low-resource language, across multiple evaluation strategies and prompt formulations. We find that LLM-human agreement varies substantially across dimensions: alignment is stronger for structured TTCT-derived properties such as Originality, Fluency, and Elaboration, but considerably weaker for more subjective dimensions, particularly Emotion and Attractiveness. Judgments are also sensitive to prompt formulation, while few-shot prompting, ensembling, and multi-agent debate provide no consistent improvement. Motivated by this dimension-dependent behavior, we investigate whether structured creativity dimensions can instead be approximated using simple, interpretable proxy metrics. We introduce CLIN, which evaluates three TTCT-derived dimensions separately using topic-aware novelty for Originality, contextual lexical clustering for Fluency, and lexical diversity for Elaboration. These proxies achieve human alignment comparable to or better than the strongest zero-shot LLM judge in our setting while requiring substantially lower evaluation cost.
2608.30754.paper_summary_zh: 評估大型語言模型 (LLM) 輸出中的創造力仍然具有挑戰性，因為創造力是多維的且以人為中心。我們檢視 LLM 如何在多種評估策略和提示格式下，可靠地評估波斯語的短篇文學文本，這是一種資源匱乏的語言。我們發現 LLM 與人類之間的協議在不同維度上有顯著差異：對於結構化的 TTCT 衍生特性，如原創性、流暢性和詳細性，協議較強，但對於更主觀的維度，特別是情感和吸引力，則明顯較弱。判斷也對提示格式敏感，而少樣本提示、集成和多代理辯論並未提供一致的改善。基於這種依賴於維度的行為，我們研究是否可以使用簡單且可解釋的代理指標來近似結構化的創造力維度。我們引入 CLIN，該指標分別使用主題感知的新穎性來評估原創性，使用上下文詞彙聚類來評估流暢性，以及使用詞彙多樣性來評估詳細性。這些代理指標在我們的設定中達到了與最強的零樣本 LLM 評判者相當或更好的人工對齊，同時所需的評估成本顯著較低。
